content: 1. Rifabutin is indicated for the prevention of disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) disease in patients with advanced HIV infection. The recommended dose is 300 mg orally once daily. If nausea, vomiting, or gastrointestinal upset occurs, the dose can be adjusted to 150 mg orally twice daily with food. 2. For treatment of disseminated MAC disease, rifabutin is administered at 5-10 mg/kg orally once daily, not exceeding 300 mg per day. Alternatively, it can be given 2-3 times per week in combination with other antitubercular agents, ensuring the dose does not exceed 300 mg per administration. 3. Rifabutin has an orphan drug designation for the treatment of disseminated MAC disease and pediatric Crohn's disease when used in combination with clarithromycin, rifabutin, and clofazimine. 4. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of apixaban by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to reduced anticoagulant effects. Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, which may result in decreased antimalarial efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of cabotegravir by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Cabotegravir is metabolized by UGT1A1 and UGT1A9 enzymes, and strong inducers of these enzymes can reduce systemic exposure, potentially leading to loss of virologic response. Rifabutin can be co-administered with oral cabotegravir but is contraindicated with Cabenuva (cabotegravir/rilpivirine) extended-release injectable suspensions. 7. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of cariprazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. CYP3A4 is responsible for the formation and elimination of cariprazine's active metabolites, and the effect of CYP3A4 inducers on cariprazine exposure has not been fully evaluated. 8. Clarithromycin increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers may reduce cobimetinib systemic exposure by more than 80%, significantly reducing its efficacy. 10. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest as contraception while on strong CYP3A4 inducers due to reduced contraceptive efficacy. Estradiol valerate/dienogest should not be used for at least 28 days after discontinuation of the inducer. 11. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of doravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered, the doravirine dose should be increased to 100 mg twice daily (approximately 12 hours apart) for the duration of rifabutin co-administration. 12. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may reduce the therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir. 13. Rifabutin decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and potential resistance. 14. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Co-administration is contraindicated as P-gp inducers reduce sofosbuvir levels and its conversion to the active metabolite GS-331007, which is responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. 16. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 17. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A inducers should be discontinued for three plasma half-lives before initiating lorlatinib. 18. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended as it may reduce the effectiveness of lumacaftor/ivacaftor. 19. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of mavacamten by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 22. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may reduce the efficacy of Viekira Pak. 23. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Rifabutin reduces the levels of panobinostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce panobinostat levels by approximately 70%, leading to treatment failure. 25. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of regorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease regorafenib levels and increase exposure to its active metabolite M-5. 26. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of roflumilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended as it may reduce therapeutic effectiveness. 27. Rifabutin decreases the levels of vandetanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated as it reduces exposure to vandetanib by up to 40%. 28. Rifabutin reduces the levels of voriconazole by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Voriconazole also increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 29. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 30. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If a strong CYP3A inducer must be used, increase the acalabrutinib dose to 200 mg twice daily. 31. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 32. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of alpelisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 33. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 34. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of amiodarone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 35. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 36. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of apremilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP inducers is not recommended as it may result in loss of efficacy. 37. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 38. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 39. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 40. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of avapritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 41. Rifabutin decreases the levels of axitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 42. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 43. Rifabutin decreases the levels of BCG vaccine live by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 45. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended as it may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance. 46. Rifabutin reduces the levels of bosutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 47. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 48. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 49. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of buspirone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 50. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If a strong CYP3A4 inducer is required, increase the cabozantinib dose as per prescribing information. 51. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 52. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of capmatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 53. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 54. Rifabutin reduces the levels of ceritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 55. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 56. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 57. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 58. Rifabutin increases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for increased antiplatelet effects when co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. 59. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of clozapine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 60. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of colchicine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 61. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 62. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 63. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (vaginal) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 64. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of copanlisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 65. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of cortisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used.
